Class MessageEnvelope

java.lang.Object
grafiosch.gtnet.m2m.model.MessageEnvelope
public class MessageEnvelope extends Object
Wrapper for all machine-to-machine (M2M) communication between GTNet instances. Every HTTP request/response between peers is wrapped in a MessageEnvelope, providing:
  • Sender identification (sourceDomain)
  • Reply correlation (souceIdForReply links to the sender's message ID)
  • Message type and parameters (messageCode, gtNetMessageParamMap)
  • Optional arbitrary payload (JSON node for type-specific data like GTNet during handshake)

  • Method Details

    • forExchange

      public static MessageEnvelope forExchange(GTNet sourceGtNet, byte messageCode, tools.jackson.databind.JsonNode payload)
      The envelope of a machine-to-machine payload exchange: an intraday or historical price request, a push, a coverage or metadata lookup, an exchange sync.

      These are not messages of a conversation. No row is written for them, so the envelope names no sender-local message; the answer comes back in the same HTTP response and is read by GTNetResponseValidator. The one factory exists because every one of these senders needs exactly the same five fields, and a sender that forgot one of them was refused by the peer for the whole release — the receiver reads the timestamp as UTC, which is what GTNetTime guarantees here.

      Parameters:
      sourceGtNet - the local GTNet entry, which supplies the domain and the busy flag
      messageCode - the wire value of the code being sent, declared transientSend() in the protocol
      payload - the request payload, already converted to a tree
      Returns:
      the envelope to post to the peer
